issues.legal_issue: A delegated marking system may guide an expert commission when it evaluates statutory criteria, provided it does not make the commission’s independent judgment illusory.
material_facts: The statute assigned the commission the task of advising on exemptions for qualifying farms and permitted rules to guide that task.
The rule assigned marks for features directed to farm management and production, and the commission retained discretion to evaluate the listed features.
issues.conclusion: The marking system was not foreign to the statute and did not fetter the commission’s discretion or make its independent judgment illusory.
issues.legal_principle: Sections 32K(1)(iv) and 32P(4) and (5) of the PEPSU Tenancy and Agricultural Lands Act allowed rules to provide objective guidance to the commission. A marking system was permissible insofar as it addressed the statutory conditions for exemption and left the commission discretion in evaluating the relevant features. The judgment relied on no earlier cases for this issue.

predicates.constitutional_writ_challenge: A party brings a constitutional writ proceeding challenging the validity of a delegated rule.
predicates.delegated_marking_system_guides_statutor: The rule assigns marks for features that evaluate the statutory conditions relevant to the decision entrusted to the commission.
predicates.commission_retains_evaluation_discretion: The commission remains free to evaluate the listed features rather than being bound to award predetermined marks.

issues.definition: When a delegated marking system guides a commission on statutory factors while leaving it evaluation discretion, the system is permissible guidance that does not make its independent judgment illusory.

issues.legal_issue: A prescribed yield standard is not invalid as unattainable or mala fide when the evidence does not establish that the standard is unreachable or was designed to defeat the statutory exemption.
material_facts: The rule prescribed crop-yield standards and treated a farm meeting 80 per cent of the prescribed marks as qualifying for full exemption.
The evidence included lower average yields but also showed that the statutory exemption depended on production high enough that breaking up the farm would cause production to fall.
The petitioners did not establish that the relevant standards, assessed in light of the reduced threshold and the evidence, were unattainable or had been fixed to defeat the exemption.
issues.conclusion: The challenge that the yield standards were unattainable and that the schedule was a mala fide exercise of rule-making power failed.
issues.legal_principle: Under section 32K(1)(iv) of the PEPSU Tenancy and Agricultural Lands Act, the likelihood that breaking up the farm would reduce production was a statutory condition for exemption. The Court considered the evidence and the practical effect of the 80 per cent threshold and held that the petitioners had not discharged their burden of establishing an unattainable standard or mala fide rule-making. The judgment relied on no earlier cases for this issue.

predicates.constitutional_writ_challenge: A party brings a constitutional writ proceeding challenging the validity of a delegated rule.
predicates.prescribed_yield_standard_assessed_with_: The court assesses the prescribed yield in light of the threshold that actually permits a farm to qualify for exemption.
predicates.evidence_does_not_establish_unattainabil: The evidence does not establish that the yield standard cannot be reached or was fixed to defeat the statutory exemption.

issues.definition: If a challenged yield standard is assessed with its effective qualifying threshold and the evidence does not establish that it is unattainable, the standard is not invalid on that ground.

issues.legal_issue: A rule cannot create an intermediate category of partial exemption when the governing statute permits only exemption of the whole qualifying farm or application of the ceiling to the whole farm, and an inseverable rule containing that category is invalid as a whole.
material_facts: The statute provided that the ceiling did not apply to a farm meeting the statutory exemption conditions, without providing for partial exemption of a qualifying farm.
The rule created an intermediate category under which only part of a farm was treated as efficiently managed and exempt.
The intermediate category was integrated with the rest of the rule and could not be excised without leaving a rule that the rule-maker might not have framed.
issues.conclusion: The intermediate category was ultra vires, and because it was inseverable, the whole rule and its accompanying schedules had to be struck down.
issues.legal_principle: Section 32K(1)(iv) of the PEPSU Tenancy and Agricultural Lands Act provided for exemption of a qualifying farm, not partial exemption of an intermediate category. A rule exceeding that authority was ultra vires; where the offending provision was integrated with the remaining rule and could not be severed, the whole rule fell. The judgment relied on no earlier cases for this issue.

predicates.constitutional_writ_challenge: A party brings a constitutional writ proceeding challenging the validity of a delegated rule.
predicates.statute_provides_only_whole_farm_exempti: The governing statute provides for exemption of a qualifying farm as a whole and does not authorize partial exemption.
predicates.delegated_rule_creates_partial_exemption: The delegated rule creates an intermediate category in which only part of a farm receives the statutory treatment.
predicates.partial_class_is_inseverable: The intermediate category is integrated with the rest of the rule and cannot be removed without disrupting the rule as a whole.

issues.definition: If a delegated rule creates an inseverable partial-exemption category that the statute does not authorize, the entire integrated rule is invalid.

issues.legal_issue: A rule requiring annual reconsideration of exemptions must be read subject to a statutory requirement that the commission advise on those exemptions and that its advice bind the government.
material_facts: The statute made the commission’s advice on exemptions binding on the government.
The rule provided for annual revision of farm classifications but did not expressly provide for consultation with the commission during revision.
The Court accepted that the rule had to be read subject to the statutory requirement and that the government was bound to obtain and follow the commission’s advice at revision.
issues.conclusion: The government was required to obtain and follow the commission’s advice when revising classifications, notwithstanding the rule’s silence on consultation.
issues.legal_principle: Sections 32P(4) and (5) of the PEPSU Tenancy and Agricultural Lands Act required the commission to advise on exemptions and made its advice binding on the government. A rule was to be read subject to those statutory requirements. The judgment relied on no earlier cases for this issue.

predicates.constitutional_writ_challenge: A party brings a constitutional writ proceeding challenging the validity of a delegated rule.
predicates.statutory_scheme_makes_commission_advice: The governing law assigns the commission an advisory role on the matter and makes its advice binding on the government.
predicates.rule_provides_for_annual_reclassificatio: The delegated rule provides for annual reconsideration or reclassification but does not expressly require consultation with the commission.

issues.definition: When the governing law makes the commission’s advice binding, a rule providing for annual reclassification must be applied subject to the requirement to obtain and follow that advice.

issues.legal_issue: A delegated rule cannot authorize the government to withdraw an exemption that the statute grants to a qualifying farm when the statute provides no authority to subject that farm to the ceiling later.
material_facts: The statute stated that the ceiling did not apply to farms meeting the exemption conditions.
The rule provided for annual revision of classifications and withdrawal of an exemption if a farm ceased to be efficiently managed.
The statute contained no provision authorizing the government to return a previously exempt farm to the ceiling after its exemption had been determined.
issues.conclusion: The rule’s provision for later withdrawal of an exemption exceeded the authority conferred by the statute and was ultra vires.
issues.legal_principle: Section 32K(1)(iv) of the PEPSU Tenancy and Agricultural Lands Act excluded qualifying farms from the ceiling, and the Act contained no power to reapply the ceiling later to a farm that had obtained that exemption. A delegated rule could not supply that missing authority. The judgment relied on no earlier cases for this issue.

predicates.constitutional_writ_challenge: A party brings a constitutional writ proceeding challenging the validity of a delegated rule.
predicates.statute_exempts_qualifying_farm: The governing statute removes a farm meeting specified conditions from the ceiling or other restriction.
predicates.statute_provides_no_later_reapplication_: The governing statute does not authorize the government to reapply the restriction to a farm after its exemption has been granted.
predicates.delegated_rule_authorizes_withdrawal_of_: The delegated rule authorizes the government to withdraw an exemption that has already been granted.

issues.definition: If a statute exempts a qualifying farm but gives no authority to reapply the restriction later, a delegated rule authorizing withdrawal of the granted exemption is ultra vires.

issues.legal_issue: A mandatory mathematical yield formula is invalid when it prevents the commission from considering material differences in land quality, natural calamities, and crop rotation that bear on production.
material_facts: The rule required the commission to apply fixed yield standards from a schedule when assigning marks for yield.
The schedule distinguished irrigated from unirrigated land but did not account for differing qualities within those categories.
The formula did not allow the commission to account for natural calamities or reasonable land left fallow in crop rotation.
issues.conclusion: The mandatory yield formula exceeded the rule-making power because it prevented consideration of relevant factors bearing on yield.
issues.legal_principle: Sections 32K(1)(iv) and 32P of the PEPSU Tenancy and Agricultural Lands Act contemplated that the commission would consider factors properly relevant to whether a farm qualified for exemption. The proviso requiring mechanical application of the schedule prevented consideration of land quality, natural calamities, and crop rotation, and therefore exceeded the authority to make rules. The judgment relied on no earlier cases for this issue.

predicates.constitutional_writ_challenge: A party brings a constitutional writ proceeding challenging the validity of a delegated rule.
predicates.rule_mandates_fixed_yield_formula: The rule requires the decision-maker to apply fixed yield standards mechanically.
predicates.formula_prevents_consideration_of_materi: The required formula prevents consideration of relevant circumstances such as land quality, natural calamities, or crop rotation.

issues.definition: If a rule compels mechanical use of yield standards that exclude material production factors, the mandatory formula is ultra vires.

issues.legal_issue: A rule that cannot function as intended after its invalid mandatory yield formula is removed must be struck down as a whole.
material_facts: The rule depended on a proviso requiring the commission to apply the scheduled yield standards.
The Court held that the proviso was invalid because it compelled a mathematical approach that excluded relevant factors.
The Court concluded that the rule could not be properly worked without the proviso.
issues.conclusion: The whole rule had to be struck down after the proviso was invalidated.
issues.legal_principle: The Court applied the principle that an invalid part cannot be severed when the remaining rule cannot properly function without it. The rule-making power arose under the PEPSU Tenancy and Agricultural Lands Act, including sections 32K and 52. The judgment relied on no earlier cases for this issue.

predicates.constitutional_writ_challenge: A party brings a constitutional writ proceeding challenging the validity of a delegated rule.
predicates.mandatory_yield_formula_is_invalid: The mandatory yield formula in the delegated rule has been held invalid.
predicates.remaining_rule_cannot_function_without_f: The remaining rule cannot properly be operated as intended after the mandatory formula is removed.

issues.definition: If an invalid mandatory formula cannot be removed without making the remaining rule unworkable, the entire rule is invalid.
